title: A small shared step for SYT2 families and DEE-P Connections

sentences.text: We invite DEE-P Connections (DEEP) to explore collaboration with SYT2 families.
Published work suggests that altered proteins can block working proteins in both SYT2 and SNAP25 disorders; the SYT2 explanation remains a hypothesis.
The atlas infers symptom similarity at 0.36 confidence and DEEP’s SNAP25 connection at 0.45—both below 0.5, and neither confirms a formal partnership.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: CMDIR includes SYT2, while RARE-X has a SNAP25 data collection program: possible starting points for exchanging experience.
Other resources include Citizen Health, ENDD Center, ESCO, the STXBP1 Foundation Grants Program, and the Cambridge/Melbourne SYT1 research collaboration.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Confirm whether every borrowed platform, network or funding program accepts SYT2; shared biology does not establish eligibility.
Check limited eye movements and muscle-test responses—reduced electrical response size and increases after stimulation—across these communities, especially SNAP25.
Resource comparisons flag these recording gaps plus 11 other symptoms for SNAP25, 16 for STXBP1 and 15 for SYT1; request the full lists.
They also flag excess protein activity in all three, preparation for signal release in SNAP25, and unstable or misfolded proteins plus two unspecified mechanisms in STXBP1.
SNAP25 loss-of-function evidence is contested and variant-specific.
Ask whether a family network is needed and invite J. Littleton, whose work covers SYT1 and SYT2, to review the plan.
Together, send one inquiry to SLC6A1 Connect asking whether Simons Searchlight could include SYT2 families, without assuming access.
Is there a patient organisation dedicated to SYT2-related disorders?
Is there a documented, accessible SYT2 animal or cell model in the atlas?
Dear DEE-P Connections team,
Could we explore a modest collaboration?
We propose one joint inquiry to SLC6A1 Connect about SYT2 inclusion in Simons Searchlight.
Please help us check eligibility before making commitments.
Thank you for considering this first step.
[Your name], on behalf of families affected by SYT2-related presynaptic congenital myasthenic syndromes
